name: Compound-contact diagnostic ultrasound
summary: A Glasgow team built a scanner that swept a sound-echo probe over the body from many angles to draw cross-sections of abdominal masses.
description: Clinical contact pulse-echo ultrasound scanner combining measurements from multiple probe angles into a cross-sectional display.

events.statement: By the publication of their 7 June 1958 paper, Donald, Macvicar and Brown had used their compound-contact scanner on patients with abdominal conditions.
events.caveats: Earlier US, Japanese and other pulse-echo and image-display methods existed. This is a clinical application of the particular contact compound scanner, not the first medical ultrasound worldwide.
